transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2027-09-01
Start: 16:00 PST
Duration: ~45 minutes
Title: POC Weekly Sync - Onboarding & Env Readiness
Attendees: Jordan, Priya, Evan (Redwood); Aisha, Mark, Liam, Sara (NexaHealth)

[00:00:05] Jordan: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, uh uh quick check, is this time still good?
[00:00:10] Aisha: Yup yep, all good on our side. Excited to see the numbers.
[00:00:15] Jordan: Cool. Quick agenda - onboarding status, access setup, a quick pass at the perf spreadsheet, and then next steps. Priya you'll lead the perf section?
[00:00:22] Priya: Yeah I'll take that. Evan will chime in on the dedicated node tests.
[00:00:27] Liam: Quick admin, we've got peering scheduled for the 6th but need to confirm service account perms. Sara will own that, but Mark is looped in.
[00:00:35] Mark: Yep, that's correct. We're trying to avoid over-privileged SA; least privilege policy.

[00:01:05] Priya: On onboarding, we had success with the hosted API earlier this week - the inference calls worked from our dev cluster, tokens flowing. The preliminary embeddings run looked ok, but we saw higher p99 on longer contexts.
[00:01:20] Sara: Right, the long-conversation use-case (10k tokens) spiked p99 to ~1.4s per token in our tests, which is more than expected. Could be our client-side batching though.
[00:01:35] Evan: Mm, ok, two quick hypotheses: 1) prefix KV cache wasn't enabled on your client, so repeated context recompute; 2) the model selection fell back to a less-optimized variant. We'll check server logs and routing.

[00:02:10] Aisha: Can you clarify the fallback rule? Last time you mentioned automatic fallback to compatible variants when capacity's tight - what's the observable for that?
[00:02:20] Priya: Good call. The runtime routes based on latency and cost policy. If a region node is saturated or a quantization incompatible variant is requested, the router picks a compatible model which may be slower. We'll surface that in the logs, but for the pilot we can pin model version to avoid surprises.

[00:03:05] Liam: For the VPC peering, do you need us to open specific ports? Our infra team prefers minimal opening.
[00:03:12] Jordan: We only need outbound HTTPS and gRPC to the Redwood endpoints. For dedicated, you'll get a private endpoint, so peering will be between subnets. We'll send an exact network checklist.

[00:04:00] Mark: On security, legal asked for SOC2 and a KMS workflow. Where do we get the attestation?
[00:04:06] Evan: I'll drop the SOC2 excerpt and KMS integration doc in the thread after the call. We support AWS KMS and HSM-backed keys for private deployments, and for hosted we redact PII and keep audit logs.

[00:04:40] Priya: Ok jumping to perf: here's what we ran (notes). Hosted API baseline using open-model-v1 quantized run: avg latency 85ms token, p95 220ms, p99 420ms on 1k context, batch size 8. On longer sequences (~5k) p99 rose to 1.1s. Dedicated node (reserved GPU) with same model: avg 60ms, p95 150ms, p99 280ms.
[00:05:12] Aisha: Thanks, can you share the raw spreadsheet? It's helpful to see the per-run config (temp, top_k, prompt length).
[00:05:18] Priya: Yes, Jordan will share the sheet after call. Note some runs used 4-bit quant and some FP16 for comparison - the 4-bit runs show cost reductions but slightly higher p99 on tail.

[00:06:00] Sara: On the quant note, are you doing dynamic quantization at runtime or a static quant build? We need to know for image-of-ops.
[00:06:06] Evan: Static quant builds on model upload are recommended for best latency. We do support on-the-fly quantized variants but dedupe and kernel selection can differ.

[00:06:35] Mark: For our production policy we'd likely want dedicated, but cost is a concern. Any guidance on break-even?
[00:06:42] Jordan: Short answer: if you have consistent throughput across business hours and need predictable p99 SLAs, dedicated usually pays off. If it's spiky, hosted with autoscaling and caching might be cheaper. We'll model with your traffic in the spreadsheet.

[00:07:20] Priya: Also, batching configuration matters - bigger batches improve throughput but can hurt single-request latency. We tuned batch size to 8 for these runs - we can try lower batch for p99-sensitive endpoints.

[00:08:05] Aisha: One more on observability - can we get per-route token-level breakdown and per-model tracing? Our auditors want traceability to prompt versions.
[00:08:13] Evan: Yes, Redwood Console exposes per-route token and model traces, plus an eval hook. We can provision longer retention for pilot if needed.

[00:09:00] Liam: Ok, back to access: Sara will create the service account and give only network/peering and minimal IAM. Any specific role names?
[00:09:08] Jordan: We'll send a role template - typically need a role that can post to the inference endpoint and read S3 for prompt artifacts if you're storing prompts. No admin perms required.

[00:10:00] Priya: Quick note on KV cache: enabling prefix cache reduced token compute by ~20% on our internal runs for repeated contexts. If you have long multi-turn, enable it client-side; we can walk through the SDK snippet.

[00:11:00] Sara: Great - we had errors when enabling the cache earlier, maybe a header mismatch. We'll share logs.

[00:12:20] Evan: If you paste the error trace to the thread we'll triage. Often it's an auth header timeout or cookie mismatch.

[00:13:05] Jordan: Switching to next steps and timelines. We want to run a dedicated smoke test once peering is up: Priya/Evan will trigger a quantized load test and capture p99/throughput.
[00:13:18] Priya: For the smoke test we plan a 30-min steady-state load with mixed prompt lengths, 70% short, 30% long, and measure token/s, p50/p95/p99. We'll also run a latency-SLO sweep for batch sizes 1,4,8.

[00:14:00] Aisha: Good, will that require any data sharing? We plan to use synthetic prompts initially.

[00:14:05] Priya: Synthetic is fine - helps isolate infra. For quality regression, later we can run a small holdout of your real prompts but redacted.

[00:15:00] Liam: On the peering window - suggested test window? We prefer off-peak, maybe 2am-4am PT.

[00:15:06] Jordan: We can do off-peak; we'll coordinate. The dedicated instance lane is tolerant.

[00:16:12] Mark: Any unexpected constraints from your side for dedicated? Disk space, particular GPU types?

[00:16:18] Evan: We recommend A100 or H100 for high throughput; A100 handles most workloads well. For quantized 4-bit workloads, we can run efficiently on T4-like instances but p99 will differ. Disk isn't heavy unless you stream big prompt artifacts.

[00:17:05] Sara: Question on data residency - we need logs kept in EU for certain workflows. Is that supported?

[00:17:12] Jordan: Yes, for Private and Dedicated we can pin region and enforce EU-only logging. Hosted can be regionally restricted as well but we'd want to confirm the contract.

[00:18:00] Priya: Back to perf anomalies: We'll pull the router logs to see whether your requests were hitting fallback variants and check whether cache headers were set.

[00:18:25] Aisha: Also the p99 numbers we saw might be amplified by client-side retries - we were seeing doubled calls in some paths. We'll audit that.

[00:19:00] Evan: If retries are the issue, you can set idempotency keys on the request and set exponential backoff. We have SDK defaults but you can override.

[00:20:10] Jordan: Quick product note: Redwood Optimize can recommend batching and quantization profiles automatically if you feed it workload traces. Might be useful post-proto.

[00:20:20] Mark: Good to know. Would that require sharing production traces?

[00:20:25] Jordan: Only a sample and redaction; we can do it in-house under NDA.

[00:21:00] Priya: Ok, I'll describe the exact smoke test steps so Liam/Sara know what's needed. Step 1: confirm peering and SA; 2: provision dedicated instance with pinned model; 3: run 30-min steady-state (script provided); 4: collect p50/p95/p99 token metrics and profiler traces; 5: send results back.

[00:22:05] Sara: We'll aim to have SA and peering ticket by Monday (9/6). I'll paste the ticket number in the thread.

[00:23:00] Jordan: On the legal side, Mark - you mentioned timeline?

[00:23:05] Mark: We're aiming to complete review within two weeks; pilot contract is small but need security appendix.

[00:23:30] Evan: We'll attach the security appendix and SOC2 artifact when Jordan posts the spreadsheet.

[00:24:00] Aisha: Any blockers on your side for running the dedicated smoke test?

[00:24:05] Priya: No blockers; we just need the peering and SA. Also confirm which model you want pinned - we used open-model-v1 in these tests.

[00:24:45] Aisha: Let's pin open-model-v1 quant as first run, then try FP16 for comparison.

[00:25:10] Priya: Perfect. We'll note both variants in the sheet.

[00:26:00] Jordan: Quick note - if you want to test failover behavior, we can simulate a region saturate and show fallback routing. Good to validate graceful degradation.

[00:26:12] Mark: Yes we'd like to see that, particularly how latency and error rates respond.

[00:27:00] Evan: We'll prepare a small demo script for failover and include expected telemetry outputs.

[00:28:20] Sara: On the SDK side, we had an issue parsing streaming tokens earlier which caused the client to hang. Any known SDK regressions?

[00:28:28] Priya: There was a small bug in the 1.2.4 client streaming parser; upgrade to 1.2.6 and it should be stable. We'll send the exact upgrade command.

[00:29:10] Jordan: Ok, let's recap next steps - Jordan will send perf spreadsheet and role template today; Evan will post SOC2 excerpt; Priya will run smoke test once peering is confirmed; Liam/Sara will create service account and confirm peering; Mark will track legal review.

[00:29:45] Aisha: Sounds good. One ask - can you include a note on cost buckets so we can estimate pilot monthly run?

[00:29:52] Jordan: Yes we'll annotate the sheet with per-token cost and reserved capacity monthly estimate.

[00:30:20] Priya: Also we'll include an optional quantization recommendation: 4-bit for cost sensitivity, FP16 for latency SLO.

[00:31:00] Mark: Ok thanks all. Anything else?

[00:31:05] Liam: One small ask, can you send the SDK snippet to enable prefix KV cache? That'll help us reproduce.

[00:31:12] Evan: Will do.

[00:32:00] Jordan: Alright let's close with action items in the thread. Thanks everyone for the quick sync.

[00:32:06] Aisha: Thanks all.

[00:32:10] (call ends)

Recap / Final next steps post-call:
- Jordan: share perf spreadsheet (with cost modeling) + role template + SDK snippets (KV cache, streaming fix).
- Evan: SOC2 excerpt, KMS/HSM integration doc, SDK upgrade command.
- Priya: Run dedicated quantized smoke test once peering is confirmed; capture p50/p95/p99 and traces.
